Extremely Frustrating User Experience
Worst User Interface in 20 Years on Steam: The menus are a convoluted, anti-consumer nightmare. Basic options are deeply buried, and somehow failed to put a straightforward "Quit to Desktop" option on the main title screen.

Aggressive Online Account Shoveling: The game relentlessly forces you to create and log into an external "Capcom ID" account every single time you boot it up. Even if you just want to play offline against bots, it constantly stops you with corporate logins.

Forced Onboarding and No Freedom: It completely disregards player control. It traps you inside specific modes and aggressively demands you use a character creator before you can back out or just play a traditional match.

Terrible Visual Execution: The graphic interface is completely obscured and illegible right out of the gate. On top of that, the artistic direction pushes jarring, visually mismatched character aesthetics that feel heavily driven by a corporate checklist rather than good taste.

Zero Respect for the Classic Fighting Experience: If you just want to log in, select a traditional roster character, pick a tier, and fight against CPU bots (like Mortal Kombat), this game forces you to jump through a dozen frustrating, unnecessary social-hub hoops first.

citations.review_text:
Relatively easy to get into. It might take a while to master the basics and then a while to find a character that suits you and then mastering that character, but I've enjoyed getting my ass kicked the whole time.

I've not had any major technical difficulties with SF6, both from the game itself nor from leverless controller plugging in. Good stuff.

Wish it wasn't OVER A HUNDRED GIGABYTES tho

The last Street Fighter game i played and owned was on the PS3, So i was looking forward to playing this as it does look good, BUT, Online mode Feels like games of Chance, getting lucky hits here and there and it gets very repetitive after about 5-6 hours, 

The controls are nothing like i experienced growing up as this Street Fighter game has 1 button specials etc, as the game mothers you and it literally holds your hands while playing it.

It feels like there is zero skill involved and i even chose "Classic Controls" thinking they were like the original Arcade controls as that's how i know street fighter, but i quickly found out they are NOT Classic Controls as i remembered, but i did persevere with it and give it a good go. 

Also its not worth the 100+GB of space needed on my SSD for such a small feeling game, 

It feels very low effort compared to the original street fighter games i grew up with and they blow this out of the water even today so i will stick with the MAME version's as this was the last time of me playing SF6 and my honest review on it.

There are some nice touches with the SNK characters and Metro City (Final Fight City) what we can walk around in SF6, but again, this is a boring street fighter in my opinion and feels very empty, (Maybe because i didn't buy all the DLC)

The DLC characters are way over priced and I'm glad i got bored of this before i spent a lot of money on Terry Boggard and Akuma, i don't think i will be playing it again.

It's such a shame as it does have a lot of potential as the graphics are decent but the character's styles are sooo bad, Blanka looks really silly compared to what we got back in the 90's, it could have been so much more fun but Capcom definitely dropped the ball on this one - Solid 5/10

citations.review_text: Great addition to the Street Fighter series. Feels so smooth compared to the older arcade Street Fighters, and maintains some kind of integrity compared to Street Fighter 5 (which would literally have ad breaks before a match). My only complaint is that you cannot purchase single characters, instead you're forced to purchace these character packs that usually include 2 or 3 characters that you will never play. Overall it's a wonderful game that was lovingly crafted, however it suffers from some questionable DLC decisions. UPDATE: I didn't know about fight coins lol

The micro transactions for characters ($7 per fighter), fight stages, single outfits, music tracks, land separate transactions for outfit colors are sucking the life out of this game. It doesn't help that the single player aspect equates to the developers laughing at you for even considering that concept.

I only bought this game cause a friend from school wanted to play it with me, but owning Street Fighter 6 makes me feel like a disgrace and its a disappointment to call this game a sequel to the amazing game that is 3rd Strike. I could go on about the problems that people already have about this game like the throw loops and the character buffs and other stuff like that, but i think that paying $30, $40, almost f**king  50 dollars just for 4 characters! and having to pay $10 for 1 character in fight coins! and then the roster is so booty cheeks. as a direct sequel to 3rd strike there is barley any Sf3 characters. There is only 2 characters from street fighter 3 those being Elena and Alex AND I AM NOT EVEN GONNA GET INTO WHAT GROSS STUFF ALEX DID IN THIS GAME, Like i want Makoto who is my GOAT and Q and literally anyone's from sf3, They could at least have added Dan cause he's awesome! I feel like i should have compensation for owning and playing this game. ALSO if Capcom ever adds Makoto to this game if they ruin her somehow i swear to GOD

Prácticas predatorias de Capcom con este juego. La edición base del juego proporciona un plantel ridículo, lleno de personajes nuevos, sin ningún carisma y sin más valor que el aportar estereotipos inclusivos, para vender después los luchadores de Street Fighter de toda la vida en DLC's de 4 personajes por año, 1 interesante y 3 pesos muertos en la mayoría de los casos, también cabe la posibilidad de comprar los personajes por separado dentro del juego, pero tampoco considero que esto sea algo para agradecer.
No lo recomiendo para nada.

[h1]Great DLC simulator called a fighting game[/h1]

I really love fighting games as much as I love Capcom, but this thing is literally an Assassin's Creed game wrapped in a "Street Fighter" skin. 

Let me start from the beginning:
I bought SF6 because I got tired of the braindead playstyle in Tekken 8, and I wanted something more defensive and reliant on technique rather than on mashing. And I kinda got what I wanted, even though I'm still learning this game (surprising, because I don't really want to, and I'm just trying to give this game a chance). 

I don't have anything to say against the gameplay- it's perfect. The graphics look sick too, and the character design is the most badass I've ever seen. But that's where the problem starts.

If you want to see a badass guy screaming "Isshun Sengeki!", you must pay. If you want a beautiful girl doing magic tricks in a fight, you must pay too. If you mained M. Bison in SF5 and want to continue maining him in SF6, you need to pay again, even though the base game already costs $40. Capcom is literally milking this game in all ways possible, and it seriously interferes with the basic gameplay experience, because 12 out of 30 characters are locked behind a paywall. Even if you don't care about locked character customization, interface customization and literally everything customizable, you still need to pay another $76.14 just to use the full roster(counting the upcoming year 4).

There is a lot of good things about this game, but Ubisoft type of playerbase treatment is ruining the game's identity

[h1]Cons :[/h1]
• money-hungry dev team
• Matchmaking server issues or whatever thing that cause forever-long queue times despite the huge player base.

I like this game, but i don't recommend it

[h1] K-HO [/h1]
This is a super fun evolution of the Street fighter franchise. The base game is awesome, and worth the price, but the DLC's get hella-expensive. r/patientgamers wait for sale to purchase. You can avoid DLC-packs by buying items using the in-game store. There's also a currency you earn with challenges - Drive tickets - and the bought currency used for exclusive items. There's weekly, monthly and daily challenges.  

Classic vs. Modern controls is a total preference thing, and can be leaning towards introducing newer players to the game. Modern is much flatter compared to Classic 6-button fighters vs. 3 buttons, and a special attack button.. Modify your controls.. .In fact, go over all the settings you have access to in this game to get the best possible experience.

At first it all looks very complex, but you ease into it. The character/avatar creation is incredibly complex. You could create yourself if you really wanted. The open world is full of unique characters and it's beautiful to see all the different faces, and their outfit variations really do a number on the uniqueness of this title. You will use each street fighter to teach your avatar their moves and build up your character while levelling up [Max Lvl. 100]. Explore the environment with moves you learn from your sensei too, and fight the people in the surrounding, or initiate fights on them, or the bad guys with the moves you learn. Avatar battlehub should be avoided till you have your perfect fighter/capable of doing some moves that can face another master, etc.

It looks amazing. The fights are super responsive and look gorgeous all the way. Your avatar is in the world of Street fighter and learning from the masters, then you get battle hub with your avatar, or the masters, as well as classic mode. 
There's also V-battles, where you can emulate the real players, but don't have to take them on in real time. It doesn't count as official matches either, so it's good practice! :)) [accessed …

Recommend? I guess, but barely. This game isn't groundbreaking. It doesn't look the best. It doesn't fight the best. This avatar mode, which is cool, don't get me wrong, is a clear way for them to try and get you to purchase more garbage you won't likely want, and certainly won't need. Dude it cracks me up they are trying to get you to purchase these pieces of clothing that clip into each other horribly, so not only is it sort of scummy, it's not even good.

This game is expensive for what it is dude. I mean it is ABSOLUTELY not worth full price, at all. It's been out since 2023 and it's roster still don't feel stacked, and to even get what is available will cost you extra. 2026 now and still no definite edition out, so you're going to have to shell out extra if you're say, a Sagat player, which thankfully I am not. And from what I am seeing, NO, you can't buy characters one by one if you're only interested in one. No, you have to buy the whole over priced pack to use them.

This game got a lot going against it, and I adore fighting games, and love street fighter, been playing it since I was a little kid. The only reason this gets a recommendation at all is because I do adore the characters, and the fighting is fun, but this game was as close as it gets to a thumbs down. Get these god awful battle passes out of our fighting games. Worlds got enough garbage thanks.

I don't recommend this game because of one thing which feels pretty scummy to me : character DLC locked in training. From what other fighting games does, you can play character DLC as long as you can in training mode (but no other game mode of course). It let you understand their move and try the character as much you want to see if you want to buy it. 

Capcom has technicaly something similar with trial tickets but it's just one hour irl (not even one hour in game) to try a character. This is a joke of bandaid. Worst of all you can't practice against a DLC character you did not purchase if you lose against it in a ranked match 

This is greedy and petty in my opinion and as one the biggest fighting game, Capcom should put a good example to follow for other fighting games.

Also I dunno why I play in 2K resolution but when I go back from screen saver mode, the resolution change back to 1080p, it's very annoying

game is fun, can be frustrating at times but it can also hit like crack. gameplay isn't the issue.

This game is glaringly pay to win, a good amount of the top tiers are DLC characters. there's definitely non DLC top tiers but a majority of the best characters are DLC. labbing is important if you want to get anywhere past platinum and even if you play a non DLC top tier, you cant lab against characters you don't own. cant in good conscience recommend a game that is so blatantly pay to win.

citations.review_text: I only play single-player, and World Tour mode was great for that, but once finished there wasn't much to do. I just randomly dropped back into SF6 and they added an Arcade Avatar mode! It's perfect! Quick fights and ladders with my custom character and a bunch of stuff to unlock. This was already my favorite looking and feeling fighting game of all time, but Avatar Arcade really seals the deal for me.
Excellent game. Very balanced. Matchmaking very fast. Single player mode Open world - abit "fetch this"  "do this" type

For many reasons I genuinely cannot recommend Street Fighter 6, this game has left me frustrated way more than it made me happy with it.

First and foremost, the connectivity issues are extremely unbearable, for most of the time I literally can't get into matches because of the constant errors, even if I'm playing in battle hub in a server with good ping and latency, I actually cannot get into the matches themselves for whatever unexplainable reason.

Now the gameplay of SF6 is fun and polished, the problem is that its mechanics are, lets say dominative based, the drive impact mechanic basically negates all basic attacks and their damage but you can break it by performing rapid combo attacks, use your super arts attacks or you can save yourself with a parry/throw/block, and so all matches are basically heavy guessing "rock, paper and scissors" games. You can try out the demo and if you like this formula then you will enjoy this game but if not then its not worth it.

The world tour mode has left me completely unsatisfied from how incredibly basic, lack-luster and half-assed it was. I went in expecting nothing and got in the end one of the worst singleplayer mode experiences that I have ever played, and its a shame because Capcom legitimately were this close to inventing a successful formula similar to SEGA's Yakuza/Like A Dragon games but they had to make this whole thing a grindy ass RPG tutorial-fest for the battle hub's avatar battles (another idea that is literal garbage and will get into it later). The plot is non-existent and the gameplay sucks so bad, there is barely any unique set-pieces and the side-content is shallow and boring. (although the small little minigames were either fun or okay, nothing special).

The Battle-hub is also a wonderful concept that also has one of the worst executions ever. No matter what, this thing will always be filled with 300+ hour players that you can't improve yourself against, you will always suck against them. There are beg…

claims.claim: The game features extensive tutorials, character guides, and training tools that help beginners learn fundamentals.

citations.review_text:
I though I didn't like fighting games before SF6. I now have time in this across PC and PS5, Guilt Gear Strive, and am excited for Tokon. I just needed a fighting game that was willing to ease me into the genre so I didn't feel like the only way to learn was to trudge through Youtube guides to get comfortable playing. I do those things now because I want to improve and not out of a feeling of necessity.
It is a great starting point if you've been put off of the genre due to the learning curve. This game has extensive tutorials for beginners and single player content to test your learning against even if you have no intention of playing online. Including a v-rival mode which has the cpu use common strats used by real people online if you want that level of practice. Some of the character specific tutorials may be a little outdated with balance changes but there is enough to get started.
And it looks excellent, the animations are so smooth not just for the attacks themselves but the frames between where your character resets to their neutral animation right after getting concussed.

This is one of the best, if not the best beginner friendly fighting game out there:
- The tutorial teaches important concepts and fundamentals beyond just the mechanics
- The character guides explain the flow chart and game plan of the characters
- The training settings offer a vast array of tools, including slowing down the time, so you can troubleshoot the combos and inputs
- A huge player base ensuring you can always find someone of your level to play against

All this make this a great experience for anyone unsure if fighting games are for they or not. Besides the matches are highly enjoyable, with plenty of options and skill expressions.

The graphics is great and vibrant and for the players not inclined to MP, the World Tour mode is easily 50 hours of SP fun, plus very good combo trials, arcade mode, V-Battle and Avatar battles are enough to keep anyone entertained for hundreds of hours.

All this make this a great experience for anyone unsure if fighting games are for they or not. Besides the matches are highly enjoyable, with plenty of options and skill expressions.

The graphics is great and vibrant and for the players not inclined to MP, the World Tour mode is easily 50 hours of SP fun, plus very good combo trials, arcade mode, V-Battle and Avatar battles are enough to keep anyone entertained for hundreds of hours.
